inspection_summary: Inspected all 958 logical lines of the hash-bound normalized article, including 940 LF-delimited records and 18 form-feed page boundaries. The source develops a two-variable q-deformation, selects the diagonal t=s-1 by its pole-cancellation and classical-limit behavior, derives negative-integer and q-Bernoulli formulas, and proves convergence to the analytically continued Riemann zeta function by replacing a blocked direct Euler-Maclaurin continuation with a Fourier/incomplete-beta representation. Textual exposition is usable, but displayed mathematics contains damaged summation, inequality, derivative, periodic-Bernoulli, factorial, exponent, and fraction glyphs; every formula-sensitive unit therefore requires verification against the retained PDF before exact reuse.

accepted_units.title: Alternation and a generating function turn a divergent power sum into a finite boundary value
accepted_units.why_material: The passage isolates Euler's two-step move: first pass from zeta to a less divergent alternating series, then encode powers by repeatedly applying an Euler-type differential operator to a geometric series whose rational form can be evaluated at the boundary. It explicitly distinguishes the formal historical move from its later Abel-summability justification.
accepted_units.context_note: Lines 13-38 supply the historical problem and the distinction between the convergent Dirichlet series and the desired non-positive values. Lines 73-92 are examples, while lines 93-99 state the modern Abel-summability boundary.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on alternating-series notation, the rational generating function, and an operator action on powers. Displayed fractions and exponents are split by extraction; verify equations (1)-(3) and all exact constants against the PDF.

accepted_units.title: A second parameter separates convergence control from the zeta argument
accepted_units.why_material: The authors construct f_q(s,t) by combining q-integers with an independent exponential damping parameter. Keeping t independent makes the initial series absolutely convergent in a clear half-plane and postpones the structurally important choice of how t should depend on s.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the design bridge from Euler's power-series device to the paper's q-family; Proposition 1 immediately tests whether the construction supports meromorphic continuation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Requires the q-integer definition, the distinction between s and t, and the series in equation (4). The extracted summation glyph is damaged, so the PDF must be checked before reproducing the formula.

accepted_units.title: Binomial expansion converts the q-series into an explicit meromorphic pole decomposition
accepted_units.why_material: Proposition 1 expands each denominator binomially, interchanges the two sums, and evaluates the inner geometric series. The resulting denominators expose the complete t-pole lattice directly, making analytic continuation a change of representation rather than an opaque extension.
accepted_units.context_note: The absolute-convergence assumptions in lines 120-127 justify the initial manipulation; the pole assertion follows from the explicit denominators rather than a separate complex-analytic construction.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-sensitive: generalized binomial coefficients, double sums, and the pole lattice are spatially degraded in the extraction. The prose fixes the transformation, but exact indices and typography need PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: The same two-parameter deformation admits a beta-like Jackson-integral representation
accepted_units.why_material: The remark provides a distinct q-calculus representation of f_q, connecting the discrete series with a beta-like integral and exposing a bridge available for later comparison or generalization.
accepted_units.context_note: This is an isolated representation remark and is not used in the subsequent proof; it should remain separate from the binomial continuation mechanism.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Strong scan dependency: the displayed Jackson-integral identity has broken alignment and missing operator glyphs. Only the existence and beta-like role of the representation are reliably recoverable from prose without the PDF.

accepted_units.title: The diagonal t=s-1 is selected because singular loci cancel without creating persistent extra poles
accepted_units.why_material: Specializing the two-variable family along t=s-1 turns intersections with the pole divisor at non-positive integers into finite indeterminacies and gives the desired full classical limit. Nearby choices reveal the design constraint: t=s lacks the cancellation, while t=s-k introduces extra finite-q poles even when their residues vanish classically.
accepted_units.context_note: Lines 197-200 preview the goals. This unit includes the definition of zeta_q and the explicit comparison with alternative diagonals, including the stated unresolved dependence on t.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on seeing the diagonal in the (s,t)-parameter plane and tracking finite-q poles versus their q-to-1 limit. Verify the series definition and residue formula against the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Euler's alternating simplification does not transfer cleanly because it couples q and q squared
accepted_units.why_material: The natural q-analogue of the alternating series satisfies a relation involving both zeta_q and zeta at q squared. The extra scale coupling destroys the simple one-function reduction that made alternation useful classically, so the paper explicitly rejects this otherwise plausible route.
accepted_units.context_note: This is negative methodological evidence tied to the successful diagonal construction, not merely another formula for the same function.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Requires distinguishing the deformation parameters q and q^2 and the alternating sign convention. Exact powers and coefficients need PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Vanishing binomial factors and a singular denominator combine to produce finite values on the pole diagonal
accepted_units.why_material: Proposition 2 reads the pole set from the continued series and then evaluates zeta_q at non-positive integers. Most terms vanish because generalized binomial coefficients truncate, while the single singular term is resolved by a first-order limit, yielding a finite closed formula.
accepted_units.context_note: The result formalizes the indeterminacy announced at lines 206-218. Low-order computations in lines 292-332 illustrate rather than extend this mechanism.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Highly formula-dependent: the finite sum, generalized binomial coefficient, exceptional r=m+1 term, and inequality glyphs are degraded. Check equations (5)-(6) and the limit calculation against the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Finite-difference annihilation isolates the Bernoulli coefficient in the classical limit
accepted_units.why_material: Theorem 1 rewrites the negative-integer formula as a finite alternating binomial sum, inserts the Bernoulli generating series, and uses a derivative/finite-difference identity that kills every intermediate degree. Only the constant and degree m+1 contributions survive, producing the classical Bernoulli value.
accepted_units.context_note: Lines 333-346 define the Bernoulli convention used by the source; lines 353-442 contain the equivalence transformations and cancellation argument.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Requires exact Bernoulli sign convention, binomial sums, differential identity, and asymptotic order. The extracted display is fragmented and must be checked against the PDF before exact mathematical reuse.

accepted_units.title: Negative q-zeta values generate q-Bernoulli numbers with both a binomial recursion and a dilation equation
accepted_units.why_material: The source packages the negative-integer values into q-Bernoulli numbers, derives a closed formula including the r=0 limiting convention, and shows that the coefficient recursion is equivalently encoded by F_q(qt)=e^t F_q(t)-t e^t.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a structural consequence of Proposition 2 and Theorem 1, not part of the proof of the later global convergence theorem.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on normalization and sign choices, the exceptional B_0(q) definition, and translating a coefficient recursion into a generating-function functional equation. Verify all formulas against the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Pointwise convergence to zeta can coexist with severe finite-sum instability near a zero
accepted_units.why_material: Theorem 2 asserts convergence for every complex s except the pole. The numerical examples contrast benign convergence at s=1/2 with enormous truncation sensitivity near the first non-trivial zero, preserving an important distinction between analytic convergence and practical numerical conditioning.
accepted_units.context_note: The proof begins at line 635. The examples are evidence about approximation behavior, not verification of the theorem.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The scientific-notation exponents and truncation counts are visibly mangled in extraction, especially lines 507-515. The qualitative contrast is recoverable, but all numerical values require PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Adding a shift parameter transports the q-limit and Bernoulli-value mechanism to Hurwitz zeta
accepted_units.why_material: The remark shows that the same construction extends from n to n+a, with the classical limit becoming Hurwitz zeta and the negative-integer limit becoming a Bernoulli polynomial. It also records the deliberate scope boundary: the paper does not develop the resulting q-Bernoulli polynomials.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a stated extension without proof in this source, so it should not be represented as independently derived here.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on the shifted q-integer and Bernoulli-polynomial generating series. The extraction of equation (7) is compressed and needs PDF checking.

accepted_units.title: Integer specialization turns the q-zeta limit into a hierarchy of Lambert-series asymptotics
accepted_units.why_material: At positive integer s=k, the continued expansion reorganizes as a Lambert series with a binomial polynomial weight. Comparing its leading degree with lower-degree terms and using induction transfers zeta_q convergence into the stated asymptotic involving zeta(k).
accepted_units.context_note: The k=2 case is shown directly; the general argument relies on the degree decomposition of the binomial coefficient and inductive disappearance of lower-degree contributions.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Requires exact normalization by (1-q)^k, the binomial coefficient polynomial, and the q-Lambert denominator. Verify equation (8) and the reindexing against the PDF.

accepted_units.title: A Lambert series becomes an Eisenstein Fourier expansion whose constant term is fixed by the zeta limit
accepted_units.why_material: For even weight, the divisor-sum expansion identifies the Lambert series with the nonconstant part of an Eisenstein series. Modularity and the q-to-1 asymptotic then provide an alternative route to the constant term, linking positive zeta values with Bernoulli data; the odd-weight failure is explicitly stated.
accepted_units.context_note: The source also recalls Hecke's Dirichlet-series functional-equation route and contrasts it with the q-limit computation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Requires parity, divisor sums, q=e^{2πiτ}, modular inversion, and complex normalization constants. Several summation and exponent glyphs are broken; the PDF is mandatory for exact formulas.

accepted_units.title: Euler-Maclaurin continuation separates a polar part, finite Bernoulli corrections, and a movable remainder
accepted_units.why_material: The proof first records the classical mechanism: repeated integration by parts yields Euler-Maclaurin, and choosing an arbitrarily high remainder order moves the valid half-plane leftward until the whole zeta plane is covered, leaving only the simple pole.
accepted_units.context_note: This classical formula is the target representation that the q-limit will eventually reproduce term by term.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on periodic Bernoulli polynomials, rising factorials, derivative order, and remainder bounds. OCR substitutes control-like glyphs for several symbols; verify equations (10)-(11).

accepted_units.title: Increasing Euler-Maclaurin order cannot continue the q-sum because the exponential factor preserves the same half-plane constraint
accepted_units.why_material: Applying Euler-Maclaurin directly to the q-summand produces an explicit formula, but higher derivative order does not improve convergence: q^{x(s-1)} forces Re(s)>1 regardless of M. The source thereby identifies the exact failure that necessitates a different representation.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the decisive negative result in the proof architecture. It should be kept with the derived q-Euler-Maclaurin expression, not summarized merely as a technical difficulty.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Derivative marks and periodic-Bernoulli glyphs are damaged, and the displayed remainder is dense. The prose-supported obstruction is reliable; exact derivatives and equation (12) require the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Fourier expansion converts the blocked periodic remainder into uniformly controlled incomplete-beta modes
accepted_units.why_material: Replacing the periodic Bernoulli polynomial by its uniformly convergent Fourier series permits interchange of sum and integral. The substitution q^x=u then packages each Fourier mode as an incomplete beta integral with a uniform-in-mode bound, creating a continuation route unavailable in the original x-representation.
accepted_units.context_note: The footnote distinguishes the borrowed Fourier-expansion idea from the paper's subsequent integration-by-parts argument.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Requires the Fourier normalization, uniform convergence, the complex shift δ=2πi/log q, and incomplete-beta parameters. Equations (13)-(14) are formula-dense and need PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Repeated integration by parts moves incomplete-beta parameters and exposes an arbitrarily extendable half-plane
accepted_units.why_material: The incomplete beta integral is recursively decomposed into finitely many boundary terms plus a shifted remainder. Applying this to each Fourier mode extends the expression to Re(s)>2-M, so increasing M now genuinely enlarges the continuation domain.
accepted_units.context_note: This succeeds precisely where direct differentiation in lines 667-714 failed: the representation change makes the adjustable order alter the relevant integrability exponent.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Depends on Pochhammer factors, complex mode shifts, boundary terms, and interchange estimates. Display alignment across page breaks is degraded; exact coefficients and signs require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: The q-limit reproduces the classical Euler-Maclaurin continuation term by term
accepted_units.why_material: After taking the elementary q-to-1 limits, Fourier identities turn the beta-mode boundary terms into Bernoulli corrections and the surviving remainder into the periodic-Bernoulli integral. The resulting expression is exactly the classical formula for zeta, and arbitrary M covers the entire plane except the pole.
accepted_units.context_note: Lines 849-856 state the elementary limits needed for the transition and overlap intentionally with the preceding continuation unit; lines 892-895 record why the other two beta families vanish.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The final comparison requires exact powers of 1-q, Bernoulli/Fourier normalization, and the remainder sign. Equations and factorial glyphs are degraded, so proof-level reuse must be checked against the PDF.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: A deformation parameter is useful only when its specialization controls both singularities and the target limit
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The independent parameter t creates design freedom, but the diagonal t=s-1 is selected by a joint criterion: it makes non-positive intersections removable and avoids persistent extra poles while retaining the full classical zeta limit.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The source explicitly says the broader dependence on t is not understood; this supports a local comparison of tested choices, not uniqueness of t=s-1 among all possible deformations.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Finite-difference cancellation converts an apparent singular specialization into Bernoulli data
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Truncation at negative integers first leaves one resolvable singular term; after rescaling toward q=1, a finite alternating binomial operator annihilates intermediate degrees and isolates the Bernoulli coefficient, which can then be repackaged into q-Bernoulli recurrences.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This relation is proved for the source's specific q-zeta and Bernoulli normalization and should not be generalized to arbitrary q-analogues without checking their singular and sign conventions.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: When adjustable differentiation does not enlarge the domain, change the representation before iterating
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The classical Euler-Maclaurin proof succeeds because increasing remainder order moves the convergence boundary, whereas the direct q-version is pinned by q^{x(s-1)}. Fourier decomposition and the substitution q^x=u create beta integrals whose integration-by-parts order does move that boundary, after which the q-limit reconstructs the original classical continuation.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The transfer depends on uniform Fourier convergence, mode bounds, and formula-sensitive limit interchange established in this source; it is not a generic license to replace every blocked remainder by a Fourier expansion.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Analytic convergence and numerical usefulness are distinct properties of a deformation
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The proof establishes pointwise classical convergence, yet the near-zero examples show that enormous truncations can remain badly conditioned before eventual convergence. A valid deformation can therefore be conceptually exact while computationally ineffective in sensitive regions.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The numerical figures are illustrative and extraction-damaged; they do not provide a quantitative conditioning theorem or uniform convergence rate.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: One Lambert-series representation links positive zeta values to modular constant terms
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Integer specialization yields a scaled Lambert sum whose classical limit is zeta(k); at even weight the same sum is the nonconstant Fourier part of an Eisenstein series, so modular inversion turns the q-limit into a computation of its Bernoulli constant term.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The modular identification is restricted to the stated even weights, and the source explicitly notes the functional-equation obstruction in odd weight.

within_source_saturation: Saturated at the level of distinct source-supported mechanisms: every section from the historical construction through the proof has been partitioned, and the accepted units retain each non-redundant construction, comparison, obstruction, representation change, theorem mechanism, extension, and computational limitation. Further subdivision would mainly isolate algebraic lines from their necessary setup, repeat low-order instances, or elevate formula fragments whose exact content is unsafe without the PDF.
